item.title: Acting Classes at Laurel Hills (Aug 26, 2026)
item.description:
Intro to Acting, Improv, and Sing, Dance, Imagine!



News Published 8/26/2026 Updated 8/26/2026



In this high-energy theatre class, students will sing, dance, and act their hearts out while building essential performance skills. Through fun games, upbeat choreography, and imaginative storytelling, young performers will explore vocal technique, learn cool dance moves, and bring characters to life using their voices and bodies. It’s the perfect place to play, create, and shine on stage!



Date: Wednesdays, Sept. 9 -30 and Oct. 7 - 28
Time: 5 - 6 p.m.
Age: 7 - 12
Cost: $60
Register on RecLink



A beginner-friendly class for adults to explore the basics of stage acting in a fun, supportive environment. Through theatre games, improvisation, and guided exercises, students build confidence, develop stage presence, and learn foundational acting skills.
No experience needed, just come ready to try something new!



Date: Wednesdays, Sept. 9 -30 and Oct. 7 - 28
Time: 7 - 8 p.m.
Age: 18 and up
Cost: $60
Register on RecLink



Laugh & Play Together! Join Raleigh Little Theatre for a lively one-hour Improv Workshop and enjoy a time of laughter, imagination, and connection. 



Explore the basics of improvisation in a fun, supportive environment—no scripts and no pressure! You’ll create spontaneous characters, play engaging games, and build confidence while learning the art of thinking on your feet.  Perfect for all experience levels!



Date: Thursdays, Sept. 17 and Oct. 15
Time: 6:30 - 7:30 p.m.
Age: 8 - 12
Cost: $15

item.title: Save a Life Day (Aug 26, 2026)
item.description:
Save a Life Day is an overdose prevention training and resource fair designed to connect community members with information, education, and resources that can help prevent overdose and save lives.



The event brings together local partners committed to overdose prevention and harm reduction and provides an opportunity for residents to learn more about how they can play a role in responding to the overdose crisis in our community.



Whether you are a community member, caregiver, service provider, or simply interested in learning how to better support others, Wake County Save a Life Day offers an opportunity to increase awareness, build practical knowledge, and connect with local resources.



Location: Greg Poole Jr. All Faiths Chapel
1030 Richardson Drive, Raleigh, NC 27603
Date: Thursday, Sept. 24
Time: 5 - 7 p.m.
Ages: 14 and up
Cost: Free
Register for Save a Life Day

item.title: Big Sweep Trash Cleanup (Aug 18, 2026)
item.description:
One of the program's oldest sites, Walnut Creek Wetland Park has been participating in the Wake County Big Sweep for decades. We rely on volunteer power to help keep our streets, park, and waterways clean! We can support over 100 volunteers for this event and all ages are welcome; bring your family, friends, youth group, or work colleagues! We often collect 2000+ pounds of garbage during this fun, satisfying event. 



Please contact Celia.Lechtman@raleighnc.gov and Rachel.Vannoordt@raleighnc.gov if you are interested in a private registration link for your group.



Location: Walnut Creek Wetland Park
Date: Saturday, Sept. 5
Time: 9 a.m. - Noon
Ages: All
Cost: Free

item.title: Join Us for the Chavis–Dix Strollway Public Meeting on August 20 (Aug 18, 2026)
item.description:
Preserving history helps connect people with previous generations and provides lessons for the future. That’s where the Chavis-Dix Strollway comes in. The 1.3 mile Strollway will become Raleigh’s second cultural trail, featuring streetscape improvements, wayfinding signage, and interpretive elements that honor the community’s history. The city’s first cultural trail – the South Park Heritage Trail – is fully funded and currently in the design development phase.



Now partially funded, the Strollway is being advanced as a concept plan. Once complete, it will create a walkable, meaningful connection between two of Raleigh’s most cherished parks: Dorothea Dix Park and John Chavis Memorial Park. It will also expand the storytelling that celebrates our city’s rich cultural heritage.



As momentum builds, the Fourth Ward Association recently hosted a bus tour on Aug. 13 highlighting the history and heritage of Raleigh’s Third and Fourth Wards – stories that will be woven throughout the Strollway. The event drew an enthusiastic crowd and showcased the community’s excitement for what’s ahead.



If you’re interested in learning more, we invite you to join us for the next public meeting on Aug. 20 from 5:30 - 7:30 p.m. at the Greg Poole Jr. All Faiths Chapel (1030 Richardson Dr., Raleigh). We’ll begin with a project overview at 5:45 p.m., share the vision and scope of the Strollway, and present draft concepts and timelines. Most importantly, we want to hear your stories and experiences – your input will help shape the interpretive elements and wayfinding features along the trail. An online survey will be available after the meeting for additional feedback.



We hope to see you there! For more news and updates on Downtown Raleigh projects, please visit our website.
